title: the operator close refuses a hand over ssh
intention: The trouble device's operator close refuses a clear whose measured hand came over ssh, Akien's included, until CC has its own ssh key (outline 17.2.2).
why: Measured 2026-11-18 on akiendelllinux: an ssh login's shell sits in session-4397.scope, which the artifact door's classify() reads as akien, and CC on akienasus logs in with the key Akien's own ssh would use (Q#115, CairnCommons/questions/open-0bfaf0f5aa8b.json). A clear's hand is artifact.caller() (cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py clear_trouble), and an operator-class hand closes a trouble past its notified set (ticket 1c1b18bac2eb), so CC over ssh could close a trouble as Akien. Akien answered 2026-11-18: until CC's key lands, approve and the operator close refuse any sshd-session caller, Akien's included. The approve half is ticket a9cf64d1f92e, PROVED; it added caller()'s ssh field.
traces_to: Law 6: the operator close is an owner's power, and a CC classed akien over ssh wields it ambiently. Outline 17.2.2 (-amm).
how: In TroubleDevice.clear (cairn/devices/trouble/trouble.py), the operator close `if isinstance(hand, dict) and fold(hand.get("class") or "") in OPERATORS: outstanding = []` gains `and not hand.get("ssh")`, with a comment citing outline 17.2.2 and Q#115. The clear still lands on the record (Law 7); the trouble closes only by the notified rule. A red-first proof emits clears in clear_trouble's shape into a scratch world, as cairn/devices/trouble/proofs/test_an_operators_measured_clear_closes.py does.
